title: Horse Riders & Animals
whatItIs: Horses can be frightened by noise and speed. Pass them slowly and widely, and take care with any animals on the road.
keyFacts: Pass horse riders and horse-drawn vehicles at no more than 10 mph, leaving at least 2 metres.
Don't sound your horn or rev your engine near horses.
Riders may ride in the centre of the lane on narrow roads, or in double file to escort a young horse or rider.
At a roundabout, a horse rider may keep to the left lane and signal right if they are going round.
If a herd of animals blocks the road, stop, switch off your engine and wait until they have gone.

items.label: Maximum speed
items.note: Pass slowly and be ready to stop

items.label: Minimum space
items.note: Leave more if you can, and pass wide

onTheTest.question: How should you pass a horse rider?
options: At no more than 10 mph, leaving at least 2 metres
Quickly, to spend less time near the horse
After sounding your horn to warn them
onTheTest.why: Pass slowly, at no more than 10 mph, and leave at least 2 metres. Noise and speed can frighten horses.

traps: Never sound your horn to warn a horse rider: it can frighten the horse.
At a roundabout, a rider in the left lane may be going all the way round.
Herd of animals on the road? Stop and switch off your engine.
